mount.note: MEASURED, not fitted. pitch_deg 23.8 comes from the encoder and the level frames: with the head level by eye the tilt servo reads 2068 ticks and the picture is 1.0 deg down (+-1.5), and the reference pose sits 2311 - 2068 = 243 ticks further down at 360/4096 deg a tick, which is 23.8 (scratch/neck_tilt_scale.txt, four still frames of one room, 2026-09-12). z_m 1.203 is the tape: floor to tilt axis 1.134 m (reference.axis_z_m in config/neck.json) plus the lens 0.086 m above it and 0.025 m in front, turned down by that pitch. Both replace the 26.0 / 1.23 the lidar-beam fit of 2026-09-10 voted for (scratch/depth_fit_models.py), which was owed a repeat anyway: its beams were projected at a lidar mount the tape corrected on 2026-09-12.

notes: The lens is measured: ros/calibrate.sh (45 views of a 9x6 checkerboard, rms 0.23 px, 2026-09-13) wrote the intrinsics block and set calibrated: true, and pepin.camera.optics answers from it. hfov_deg is the nominal pinhole that reader falls back to when calibrated is false — it is 82.94, the field of view the calibration measured, because the best known number is what a bad calibration must be switched off onto; it was 78.0, the lidar-beam fit of 2026-09-10, and 70 is the vendor number that put the image edges 8 deg wrong. The mount beside it is measured too: the pitch from the level frames and the encoder, the height from a tape (see the mount note). The 78 / 26 self-calibration is STALE and is not the source of any number in this file any more.
